hedges.reason: Nothing on the list expresses the Canadian heavy-oil part of my hedge thesis: there is no WCS, Alberta, Trans Mountain or Canadian oil-equity instrument. The Toronto, Vancouver and Quebec races and the US-Canada tariff ladder have no mechanical link to Gulf Coast heavy-crude competition. The closest instrument is the thesis's own driver: Rodríguez still holding power in Venezuela at year-end because Washington treats her as its working partner. That is the world where Venezuelan heavy crude flows to the Gulf and my primary basket loses. E80.2 YES pays in that world and loses when she is removed (C20 YES). This is a Venezuela instrument, not the Canada one, so it hedges the primary's main failure thread directly rather than through a different region.

claims.reason: If no listed leader leaves office permanently by 31 Dec, Rodríguez still holds the acting presidency on that date. Formal office then goes with de facto executive authority, since the armed forces and ministries report through her. The only exception would be de facto authority sitting openly with Cabello, Padrino or US officials while she stays in office, and that is a thin edge case.

If Rodríguez permanently leaves the acting presidency before 2027, she cannot be the de facto head of state at noon on 31 Dec. A caretaker stay would not count as leaving, so C20 YES means she is actually gone.
